questions.title: Grade report file
questions.prompt:
`grades.txt` starts with the number of students `n`, followed by `n` scores, one per line. Write a program that creates `report.txt` containing one line per student, numbered from 1: ``` Student 1: 73 PASS Student 2: 41 FAIL ``` A score of **50** or more is a pass. After writing the file, print `Passed:

of ` to the screen. If `grades.txt` cannot be opened, print `Error opening grades.txt` and do not create `report.txt`. Close both files.

out_files.report.txt:
Student 1: 1 FAIL
Student 2: 82 PASS
Student 3: 47 FAIL
Student 4: 21 FAIL
Student 5: 28 FAIL
Student 6: 93 PASS

questions.title: Sum the numbers in a file
questions.prompt:
The file `data.txt` contains integers, one per line (it may be empty). Write a
program that reads every integer in the file (use `fscanf` until it stops
returning 1) and prints

```
Count: <how many integers>
Sum: <their sum>
Average: <average with 2 decimal places>
```

If the file is empty, print only `No data`. If `data.txt` cannot be opened,
print `Error: could not open data.txt` and end the program. Close the file when
you are done.

questions.title: Count values above a threshold in a file
questions.prompt:
Write the function `count_above` that opens the file named `filename`, reads all
of the integers in it (separated by spaces), and returns how many are **strictly
greater** than `threshold`. If the file cannot be opened, return `-1`.
Remember to close the file.
